newsitem.title: UK: UK needs separate gas/electric watchdogs - Offer.
newsitem.headline: UK needs separate gas/electric watchdogs - Offer.

text.p: UK electricity regulator Stephen Littlechild said on Wednesday that there was a need for separate regulators in the gas and electricity industries at least through next year, when markets in both were opening up to competition.
But he agreed there could be a case for slimming down the two watchdogs in the future.
"There has been a strong case for separate regulation in the past. There's enough work to keep one regulator going (in each industry), and there are advantages in specialisation."

He said that 1998 was going to be a busy year for both industries, with the opening of domestic competition in the gas market going through the final phases, while opening of electricity market was scheduled both to start and finish in the same year.
After that, he said, "I can see there's a case for putting them together if the industries become so interlinked."

There was already an arbitrage between the gas and electricity markets, and in the future he saw independent generators looking at this more often by deciding whether to sell gas into the gas market or to burn it and sell electricity.
